picks.stageN: Closed Nov 4 at $33.40, above the $32.66 52-week high cited by the source (Nov 3 article).
picks.why: Berkshire Hathaway, a roughly 37% owner, bought 924,281 shares for about $26.9M between Oct 30 and Nov 3 at roughly $28.89 to $30.23. Alpha Vantage shows a +8.4% close on Nov 4 on 10.1M shares.
picks.risk: The stock is already up about 12.7% in a week and past its prior high, so the early window may be closing. Revenue was flat (-0.3%) in Q3.

picks.setup: Big director buy under both moving averages
picks.why: Director Dylan Haggart bought 137,500 shares on Nov 2 at about $77.12 (about $10.6M), raising his stake 7.04%. Q3 EPS was $1.37 vs $1.07 expected; P/E is 10.37 and the average analyst target is $106.25.
picks.risk: The stock sits under both averages, so the trend is still down. Other outlets report different buy totals for the same filings.

picks.setup: CEO buys the dip, stock down about half
picks.stageN: Down about 51% in a month after a 28.6% drop on Oct 30.
picks.why: CEO Lip-Bu Tan bought 150,000 shares on Nov 2 at about $64.73 (about $9.7M) through a family trust. Intel fell 28.6% on Oct 30 after a weaker Q4 outlook (revenue $15B-$16B, EPS $0.25).
picks.risk: The stock traded about 10% below his buy price within two days, and his August purchase near $95 is far underwater. Management expects PC weakness into 1H 2027.

picks.setup: CEO buy after a 17% post-earnings drop
picks.stageN: Shares fell about 17% after Oct 27 results; Nov 4 close $151.25.
picks.why: CEO Frank Lonegro bought 5,000 shares on Oct 30 at about $142.92 ($714,619), lifting direct holdings 22% to 28,110. Q3 EPS was $1.42 vs $1.67 expected, with insurance and claims costs of $55.3M vs $33M.
picks.risk: Earnings missed on rising claims costs, which could repeat. The stock has bounced above the CEO buy price already.

picks.setup: Two directors buy a beaten-down stock
picks.why: Directors Mollenkopf (2,950 shares at $173.03, about $510K) and Buckley (5,820 shares at $171.55, about $998K) bought on Oct 30. Consensus is Moderate Buy with an average target of $247.88.
picks.risk: Q3 adjusted EPS was -$0.34 vs -$0.25 expected, and Wells Fargo, Morgan Stanley and UBS all cut targets. The buys are small against the share price.

picks.cat: Q3 beat, Q4 guide above Street (Nov 4)
picks.setup: Earnings gap up with a new buyback
picks.why: Q3 revenue was $2.19B (+55%) vs $2.08B expected, EPS $4.30 vs $4.07. Q4 revenue guide is $2.365B-$2.395B vs $2.25B expected, plus a new $3.2B buyback. It closed Nov 4 at $271.75 (+10.69%) before the after-hours jump.
picks.risk: After-hours prices can fade at the open, and the stock had already risen 10.7% on Nov 4.

picks.cat: Fiscal Q1 beat, guide above Street (Nov 4)
picks.setup: Beat and raise after a down day
picks.why: Revenue was $2.37B (nearly +50%) vs $2.31B expected, EPS $2.09 vs $1.97. Q2 guide is $2.55B-$2.75B revenue and $2.28-$2.48 EPS, both above the Street. It closed Nov 4 at $195.09 (-5.91%).
picks.risk: AI-linked optical names fell with the sector on Nov 4. A weak chip tape (Qualcomm, Kospi) can overwhelm one good report.

picks.setup: Handset weakness, data center target kept
picks.why: Revenue was $10.322B (-8%) vs $10.111B expected, EPS $2.17 vs $2.16. Handset revenue fell 26% while auto rose 89%. Reuters had it down about 10% premarket Nov 5. The $5B fiscal 2027 data center target was reiterated.
picks.risk: A gap down can extend or bounce; the source gives no volume or options data. Premarket and after-hours quotes differ.
picks.srcN: Benzinga via TradingView, Nov 4; Reuters via Yahoo Finance, Nov 5

picks.why: Revenue was $1.72B (+14%) vs $1.73B expected, EPS $0.03 vs breakeven. Snap will stop reporting daily active users (495M) and switch to monthly. It closed Nov 4 at $5.92 (+5.81%).
picks.risk: Advertising revenue grew only 4% per Seeking Alpha. Reuters had it down about 10% premarket.

picks.why: Trades near $52 vs a 50-day average of $64.23 and 200-day of $79.93. Consensus EPS is about -$0.07 on revenue of about $257M. Average analyst target is $102.05.
picks.risk: Insiders sold about 400,749 shares (about $27M) over 90 days. Earnings can gap it either way.

picks.why: Fell as much as 8% on Nov 4 with no company news as Democrats won Congress. It traded at 21x forward earnings vs a three-year average of 26x, and the Google and Amazon contracts remain in place.
picks.risk: Earnings depend on new data-center contracts, and state moratoria talk could weigh on the whole group. Management has promised a second look at its $11.50-$12.50 2026 guidance.

picks.setup: Sharp drop in a strong theme
picks.why: Fell 12.9% on Nov 4 as data-center stocks sold off after the midterms. Q3 sales rose 61% to $4.3B and organic orders more than doubled, and the writer calls it a sturdier way to buy the dip.
picks.risk: Policy risk (state data-center moratoria) is not resolved. The writer suggests staging purchases rather than buying at once.

picks.cat: Q3 results Thu Nov 12 before open
picks.setup: Earnings in a week after a drop
picks.why: Annualized run-rate revenue target is $7B-$9B by year-end 2026 vs $3.0B at the end of June. Capex guidance is $20B-$25B and Microsoft has a contract worth up to $19.4B.
picks.risk: Three customers were 59% of Q2 revenue, and funding relies on stock sales and about $5.75B of convertible notes. The author chose to wait a week.

picks.why: Q3 revenue rose 12% to $201.9B with operating income up 61%. AWS grew nearly 40%, its fastest in almost five years. 42 of 60 analysts rate it Buy; the average target is $332.41.
picks.risk: Online store sales grew only 2% (vs 15% a quarter earlier) and Walmart is gaining e-commerce share. Targets were set on Oct 30 before a 6% jump.

picks.why: Google Cloud grew 103% to $30.7B in Q3 with a $561B backlog, and the Gemini app reached 1B users. It trades at about 18x forward earnings and is down 11% this year.
picks.risk: Q3 revenue ($127.6B) missed estimates and free cash flow was -$9.1B vs +$24.5B a year earlier on heavy AI spending.

picks.setup: Large ad platform with a split-like event coming
picks.why: Meta created a non-voting Class C stock; Class A holders get one Class C share per share after the Jan 19 effective date, which the article calls effectively a 2-for-1 split. It has traded between $500 and $750 for over two years.
picks.risk: A split changes the share count, not the business. The source gives no earnings or valuation figures.

picks.why: Analyst target raised from $350 to $400. AI revenue is expected to double to $115B in fiscal 2027 and $230B in 2028. Anthropic has $161B of commitments with it.
picks.risk: Growth leans on Anthropic and OpenAI, who depend on raising more money. The writer owns shares.

picks.why: About 5.3x this year's earnings, 80.7% gross margin and 107% expected growth. The CEO reportedly expects supply to stay tight through 2027 and 2028.
picks.risk: Memory booms end. Customer supply agreements may soften the next downturn but will not remove it.

picks.stageN: Real date, but the stock is down 20.8% over 30 days and the filing's acceptance is not confirmed.
picks.why: NRx has a goal date of Nov 10 for its NRX-100 (IV ketamine) application. The stock closed Nov 4 at $2.49, up 11.2% on 1.13M shares, after falling 20.8% over 30 days.
picks.risk: The calendar page says it cannot confirm the FDA accepted the filing, and it is a generic-drug (GDUFA) date. Cash and share count were not checked. A miss or delay can gap the stock down hard.
picks.srcN: BiopharmaWatch FDA calendar, Q4 2026 (price from Alpha Vantage, Nov 4)

picks.stageN: Already up 13.8% into earnings, so a good report may already be priced in.
picks.why: Opendoor reports Q3 results on Nov 5 and closed Nov 4 at $1.98, up 13.8%. It ranked among the most active sub-$5 names that day with about $102M traded.
picks.risk: Earnings gaps cut both ways, and a run-up into the report often reverses. Housing depends on mortgage rates, which are above 7%. Cash and share count were not checked.
picks.srcN: Stock Titan, earnings date; The Desperate Trader, Nov 4 price

picks.stageN: Hit above $1.90 premarket (+142%) on a proxy filing, then faded to a +55% close.
picks.why: Curis jumped as much as 142% premarket after a preliminary proxy filing that the source calls routine. Close was $1.11 (+55.5%), versus $0.71 the day before.
picks.risk: Cash was about $5.6M against a quarterly loss near $8.6M, so it will probably need to raise money, and the proxy may include more authorized shares. Source is a promotional trading site.
picks.srcN: Timothy Sykes, Nov 4; The Desperate Trader (close)

picks.stageN: Closed Nov 4 at $0.319 vs a $2.72 prior close (-88.3%) on 48.7M shares per Alpha Vantage, after the Nov 3 spike.
picks.why: Alpha Vantage shows a -88.3% day on Nov 4 after the Nov 3 spike of 60.9% on 95.1M shares vs a 515K average. A 1-for-10 reverse split on Oct 27 followed a Nasdaq notice for trading under $1.
picks.risk: A trading suspension was possible on Nov 5 and it is ineligible for the usual 180-day extension because of repeated reverse splits. A study example of a trap.
picks.srcN: TipRanks, Nov 4; MarketBeat via Stock Observer, Nov 3

picks.cat: Restructuring plan, expected by end of 2026
picks.setup: Rally on a plan that cancels the shares
picks.stageN: Up 68% on Nov 3 even though existing shares are to be cancelled.
picks.why: Mercer plans to convert about $1.1B of debt into shares, cut debt 88% and raise $400M. Volume was about 578M shares versus a 4.3M average, and the stock rose 68% to about $0.22.
picks.risk: The plan cancels existing shares and issues new ones, so current holders can be wiped out or heavily diluted, and completion is not certain. A trap for anyone buying the spike.
picks.srcN: TipRanks, Nov 4; MarketBeat via Stock Observer, Nov 3
